newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Trade data fails to sway ringgit from range.
newsitem.headline: Trade data fails to sway ringgit from range.

text.p: News that Malaysia recorded a trade deficit in October failed to sway the ringgit, which traded within its expected range.
Dealers and analysts said with speculation of a trade deficit circulating since last week, the confirmation only caused momentary weakness of the ringgit.
"When it came out, the figure wasn't unexpected," said Sani Hamid, analyst at research house MMS International.
The Statistics Department said Malaysia recorded a negative balance of 773.4 million ringgit in its October trade, contributed to by the purchase of two commercial aircraft.
Around 0915 GMT, ringgit was at 2.5240/50, up from 2.5260/70 at the end of local trading on Monday.
"It's buy (dollars) on rumour, sell on fact," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. "There's also no commercial demand to help push the ringgit along," he added.

Research house I.D.E.A said since year-end currency repatriation requirements should have already been completed, "we are not expecting the ringgit to suffer more attacks" as had happened earlier this year.
Dealers said the quiet dollar/majors due to year-end factors also kept the ringgit at stable levels.
